input: Research Boeing (boeing.com) for a hedge fund

risks.claim: Production/cash-conversion risk: the 2026-10-27 call identified wing output, North Line certification and Wichita fuselage stability as prerequisites for higher 737 rates. A large order book does not eliminate factory bottlenecks.

Margin risk: Commercial Airplanes had a negative 6.5% operating margin in Q3 2026, reflecting unfavorable delivery mix and higher projected production-adjustment and supply-chain costs. Revenue growth alone does not establish a profitable commercial-airplane recovery.

Cash-flow timing risk: the approximately $2bn 2026 FCF forecast depends on tanker-order advance timing and seasonal working capital; the 2027 outlook includes about $1bn more capital expenditure and less favorable order deposits. These dependencies were disclosed 2026-10-27.

777X schedule risk: management’s multi-year cash targets assume certification by mid-2027, while first delivery remains a 2027 target. Neither establishes a delivery catalyst before 2027-05-10; another delay would challenge the cash-recovery path. Outlook as of 2026-10-27.

output.company: The Boeing Company (NYSE: BA; boeing.com) — decision date 2026-11-10

catalysts.claim: 2026-12: Boeing plans to notify affected employees of commercial-airplane workforce reductions. The announcement targets approximately 5% through layoffs and attrition; execution and restructuring costs are near-term watchpoints. As of 2026-11-09.

Early 2027: management expects previously built 737-7 and 737-10 aircraft to begin deliveries, potentially releasing inventory cash. This is a management timing window, not a confirmed delivery day; stated 2026-10-27.

2027-03-01: Boeing’s 2.80% senior-unsecured notes mature, a refinancing/cash-use checkpoint within the investment horizon. Maturity and coupon verified on a bond reference page with pricing as of 2026-11-06; issue principal was not verified.

event_driven.claim: Spirit AeroSystems acquisition closed 2025-12-08. Boeing brought its principal fuselage/structures supplier in-house; commercial and aftermarket operations integrate into Boeing while Spirit Defense retains independent governance and operations. Integration, rather than deal approval, is the remaining execution issue.

Jeppesen ForeFlight completed its separation from Boeing and sale to Thoma Bravo in an all-cash transaction valued at $10.55bn on 2025-11-03. This is completed portfolio monetization, not an upcoming sale catalyst; transaction value as of closing.

output.research_view: As of 2026-11-10, the critical issue is execution rather than demand: the latest workforce cuts and slower production ramp temper the benefit of MAX certification and new orders. Focus on delivery-driven cash conversion and the credibility of approximately $2bn 2026 and $3bn 2027 free-cash-flow targets, rather than treating backlog or completed asset sales as recurring earnings [Boeing earnings call](https://www.fool.com/earnings/call-transcripts/2026/10/27/boeing-ba-q3-2026-earnings-call-transcript/), [Seattle Times](https://www.seattletimes.com/business/boeing-aerospace/boeing-will-cut-5-of-its-commercial-airplane-workforce/).

credit_signals.claim: As of 2026-09-30, cash and marketable investments totaled $20.7bn and consolidated debt was $45.9bn; $10bn of revolving credit facilities remained undrawn. Figures reported 2026-10-27.

August 2026 refinancing replaced the expiring $3bn revolver with a $3bn 364-day facility expiring August 2027, with a term-out option to August 2028. Amended $3bn and $4bn facilities now expire August 2029 and May 2030. Boeing reported compliance with all debt/credit-facility covenants as of 2026-09-30.

The Q3 filing reports Fitch BBB-/positive following its June 2026 outlook upgrade, S&P BBB-/stable and Moody’s Baa3/stable. These are the ratings disclosed with the 2026-09-30 quarter, not independently verified subsequent rating actions.

alternative_signals.claim: On 2026-11-09, The Seattle Times reported an employee memo targeting approximately 5% fewer Commercial Airplanes employees through layoffs and attrition and a slower production ramp. The precise layoff count was not disclosed; this is a division-level reduction, not 5% of all Boeing.

Avolon finalized an order for 140 737-10s on 2026-11-04, raising its unfilled Boeing orders above 240. Boeing said lessors had placed more than 230 firm 737-10 orders in 2026 as of that announcement; contract pricing was not disclosed.

FAA issued the 737 MAX-10 amended type certificate and updated Production Limitation Record on 2026-10-20, authorizing production and delivery. Certification is already achieved at the decision date; delivery execution is the remaining catalyst.

results_vs_guidance.claim: Q3 2026, ended 2026-09-30: revenue $24.188bn, GAAP net loss $116m, diluted loss $0.26/share and non-GAAP core loss $0.34/share; operating cash flow $1.496bn. Reported 2026-10-27.
Q3 2026 versus LSEG consensus reported on 2026-10-27: adjusted loss $0.34/share versus $0.21 expected; revenue $24.19bn versus $23.84bn expected. Revenue beat, earnings missed.

Current management outlook as of 2026-10-27: approximately $2bn free cash flow in 2026, $3bn in 2027, $6bn in 2028 and $10bn in 2029. The 2026 outlook assumes a KC-46A lot 13 order/advance and seasonal working-capital benefits; later targets assume 777X certification by mid-2027. These are forecasts, not reported results.

Against prior operational targets, management said on 2026-10-27 that 2026 737 deliveries would fall short of the 500-aircraft target and 787 deliveries should be near the low end of the unchanged 90–100 range. Targeting 52 monthly 737s in the second half of 2027 delays the cash-conversion ramp.

insider_and_ownership.claim: Director Steven Mollenkopf bought 2,950 common shares on 2026-10-30 at a weighted-average $173.026/share, bringing direct ownership to 6,717 shares. Form 4 filed 2026-11-03 identifies transaction code P: an open-market purchase, not an equity grant or tax withholding.

Capital World Investors disclosed 41,497,786 beneficially owned shares, or 5.2%, as of 2026-03-31. Its Schedule 13G includes preferred stock representing 15,370,300 common shares and certifies ordinary-course, non-control intent. This is a historical ownership snapshot, not evidence of a recent purchase.

Vanguard Capital Management reported 58,558,920 shares, or 7.45%, as of 2026-03-31 in a Schedule 13G signed 2026-04-29. Sole voting power was 7,553,263 shares; sole dispositive power was 58,558,920. The snapshot does not establish a recent position increase.
